brief.situation: You are the information security manager at Northgate Freight, a fictional logistics company. The VP Sales asks for a six-month exception from the encryption and MFA standard: 300 drivers would use a legacy scanner app that keeps customer addresses and signatures unencrypted on the handhelds, so a new contract can launch in week 3. Assess the risk against the board's appetite, decide what to recommend, and run the exception through governance.
handover: Appetite statement: customer personal data must not leave our control unencrypted. Tolerance: exceptions up to 90 days, with compensating controls, approved by the business owner and reviewed by the security steering committee.
Your discretionary budget this quarter is 40 thousand dollars.
howItWorks: The clock is the quarter: each task takes days. Choose it, then let it finish, which moves the calendar on. The business and the risk move on the same calendar.
The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words, the budget committed and the docket.
When you close the quarter you write the exception record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The fictional company's discretionary security budget for the quarter, thousand dollars.
The contract launch is in week 3.
A handheld is stolen in week 8.

writeup.question: For the exception record: how you rated the risk against the appetite, what you recommended and why, and who decided.

parts.label: Against the appetite
parts.criteria: Rates likelihood and impact from the loss history and the data held, and compares the result with the appetite and tolerance before deciding.
parts.modelAnswer: About 40 devices a year are lost, each with about 2,000 customers' data unencrypted: high, and outside an appetite that allows no unencrypted customer data outside our control.

parts.label: The recommendation
parts.criteria: Recommends an exception inside the tolerance: at most 90 days, with compensating controls (encryption, remote wipe, purge) live before the risk is, and a plan to remove the cause before expiry; neither the six months asked for nor a flat refusal that ignores the business.
parts.modelAnswer: Ninety days with full-device encryption, remote wipe and a 7-day purge, live before the launch, and the app replaced by week 12.

parts.label: Governance
parts.criteria: The business owner accepts and owns the residual risk; the steering committee reviews; the register records owner, expiry and conditions; no spend outside the budget.
parts.modelAnswer: The VP Sales signed as risk owner, the steering committee endorsed it, and the register shows the owner, the 90-day expiry and the conditions.

expertPath.text: Rate the risk from the loss history and the data held; set it against the appetite and the tolerance; work out compensating controls with IT.
Meet the VP; recommend 90 days with encryption, remote wipe and a purge; the VP signs as owner; IT rolls the controls out before the launch.
Steering committee review, register entry with owner, expiry and conditions, and a plan to replace the app by week 12.
A stolen handheld is wiped and encrypted; the exception closes on time when the app is replaced.

managed.headline: Good: inside the tolerance, owned and governed
managed.body: An exception is a time-limited, conditioned acceptance by the business owner, reviewed by governance, with the cause removed before it expires.

costly.headline: Safe, at a cost
costly.body: The criteria show what was missing: the assessment, the governance steps, or a way for the business to meet its deadline.

breach.headline: The exception let the data walk
breach.body: Without encryption and remote wipe, the first stolen handheld became a notifiable breach.

authority.headline: Not your risk to sign
authority.body: The security manager recommends; the business owner accepts the residual risk.

overspend.headline: Over budget
overspend.body: A three-times overspend outside the process is not a treatment the steering committee can stand behind.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No exception record was written before the run's limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Rate the risk from evidence: about 40 handhelds lost a year, each with about 2,000 customers' data unencrypted, so high, and outside an appetite that allows no unencrypted customer data outside our control. The tolerance allows 90 days with compensating controls approved by the business owner. Recommend exactly that: encryption, remote wipe and a 7-day purge, live before the launch, and a plan to replace the app by week 12. The VP Sales signs as owner; the steering committee reviews; the register records owner, expiry and conditions.
